_comment: THE CROSS-MODULE CONTRACT FOR ISSUE 598's RESOLVER DIGEST.
oasgen-provider DECLARES status.<statusField> on the generated CRD. rest-dynamic-controller
WRITES and COMPARES it. They are separate Go modules in this one repository, both predicates
under internal/, so they cannot share a definition -- they share this file instead, and each
module's suite asserts its OWN predicate against every row.
Two things can drift between them, and each is silent:
1. THE FIELD NAME. If they disagree, the controller writes a key the CRD does not declare,
the apiserver prunes it, the write exits 0, and the rotation is never detected -- which is
issue 598's own defect arriving through its fix.
2. THE SCOPE RULE: WHICH verb's secretRef resolvers count. A digest difference's only remedy
is an update, so only the update verb's resolvers may contribute. If the declaring side
were wider than the writing side, kinds would carry a permanently empty field; if the
writing side were wider, a create-only secretRef would report drift that no update can
ever retire -- an update per poll, per CR, forever.
`inScope` is a STATIC property of the resource's shape. A resolver's `when` guard is evaluated
per CR instance at runtime and is deliberately NOT part of this contract: a guarded resolver is
in scope for the declaration and may still contribute nothing on a given instance. The guard is
asserted on the controller side only.

cases.name: secretRef on update
cases.why: the whole point: an update can push the rotated value, so the digest has a remedy

cases.name: secretRef on update with a when guard
cases.why: a guard decides whether THIS INSTANCE resolves it, not whether the kind is in scope

cases.name: secretRef on both create and update
cases.why: the update verb's resolver counts; the create one is simply not consulted

cases.name: secretRef on create only
cases.why: THE DISCRIMINATING ROW. An update cannot push this value, so a difference in it would report drift no update can retire -- one update per poll, per CR, forever

cases.name: secretRef on create with no update verb at all
cases.why: nothing about this resource is fixable by an update, so nothing may be reported as drift

cases.name: secretRef on delete
cases.why: a delete credential is not resource content; re-deleting is not a remedy

cases.name: secretRef on a dispatch verb
cases.why: a dispatch has side effects; re-running one to retire a digest difference is not a repair

cases.name: secretRef on findby
cases.why: an observe-direction credential; its rotation changes nothing about the resource's content

cases.name: a dependentLookup resolver on update
cases.why: a resolver but not a secretRef: its value comes from an API call, not Secret content, and resolving it would reach the vendor once per CR per poll

cases.name: a plain mapping on update with no resolver
cases.why: a CR-sourced value is already in spec, so ordinary drift detection covers it

cases.name: no verbs at all
cases.why: the degenerate shape; nothing to declare and nothing to write
